visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 shows the actual projectile problem with a correctly placed parabolic trajectory, axes, launch components, and correct flight time, while Lesson 1 is more generic and its mid-frame emphasizes 34.64 m/s without enough positional context, making it less visually faithful to the full range problem.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 includes a well-formed, wired fill-in checkpoint with a real prompt, accepted answers, hint, and remediation path after a specific act, while Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no evidence of any functioning interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 provides clear, natural narration with spoken math like “v-naught-x” and no obvious raw LaTeX or garbling, while Lesson 1 has no available narration transcript and therefore cannot demonstrate any audio quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides timed visual cues that are mostly aligned with the narration despite a few early triggers, whereas Lesson 1 has no transcript or cue data at all, making its sync effectively unevaluable and worse on this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 gives a mathematically correct projectile-motion solution with appropriate decomposition, flight-time calculation, and range formula, whereas Lesson 1 has no available transcript or plan to demonstrate any correct or pedagogically useful explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 is more visually engaging and legible with a consistent sketch style and centered compositions, whereas Lesson 2 has distracting video controls, low-contrast/faded text, excessive empty space, and a mid-lesson layout pushed awkwardly to the left.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner: five of six agents prefer it, mostly with very high confidence, including visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, sync, and concept accuracy. These dimensions indicate that Lesson 2 presents the projectile-motion problem accurately, includes functional interaction, provides clear narration, aligns visuals reasonably well with narration, and gives a correct mathematical explanation. Lesson 1 only wins polish, with the agent noting stronger visual style and composition, but that single advantage does not outweigh Lesson 2's broad and high-confidence superiority across the core instructional dimensions.
